primary_findings.title: Idle-clock unit guard is one-sided but documented as fail-closed
primary_findings.why_it_matters: If `cpuInfo[].idleClock` is not microseconds on this console, CORE does not fall back to `--`. The only unit check is one-directional: `cpu_pct_from_idle()` rejects an idle delta that exceeds the elapsed time, so a counter that advances faster than wall time is caught, but a coarser counter (milliseconds, seconds, a tick larger than 1 us) passes, every per-core delta becomes a small fraction of elapsed, and the ratio renders a permanent ~100 % - the exact fabricated number D6/D103 forbid and the exact static-100 % symptom PROJECT.md's hardware checklist says must never appear, indistinguishable from a genuinely saturated machine. The stated intent for this change is to fail closed when the idle-clock unit is wrong, and four comments and docs promise a full guarantee the arithmetic does not provide. The two reviewers split on severity (P1 from project-standards against the intent contract, P2 from correctness because the unit itself is still [C] on hardware); the consequence if it is wrong is a fabricated hero number, so the cautious rating stands.

primary_findings.title: Fabricated CTX/WAKE 0/S when the cumulative counters are absent or regress
primary_findings.why_it_matters: CORE prints `CTX 0/S  WAKE 0/S` as if it had measured them whenever the CPU sample is otherwise valid. `sample_cpu()` zeroes both rates at the top of every sample and then skips the assignment when a cumulative counter has not advanced or has gone backwards; `cpu_valid` is decided by the idle clocks alone, so the caption's only validity gate stays open. The adapter sums the two counters over the cores active at read time, so a narrowing `activeCpuMask` or a 32-bit `threadSwitchCount`/`comesOutOfIdleCount` wrap makes the total fall, and zero-filled or frozen counters from firmware that does not populate them read as a measured zero. On a running Vita zero context switches per second is impossible, so the hero panel shows an invented number - exactly the zero-substitution AGENTS.md rule 6, README.md:194 and the Metrics contract forbid. Three reviewers reached the same defect and fix path; the fix is the per-field validity pattern the POWER panel already uses.

residual_risks: Catch-up sampling can feed sub-window measurements into the readout and the 20 s trace: app.c:501-506 re-runs metrics_sample_slow() up to MAX_CATCH_UP_SAMPLES (3, app.h:21) in a tight loop, so the calls after a hitch have an elapsed of only the microseconds the sampler itself takes. A genuine 0 us idle delta then reads 100 %, a single context switch becomes a five-figure CTX rate, and the sample lands in a trace whose axis assumes 100 ms windows. Host tests and the fake (fixed 100 ms step) cannot reproduce it; hardware has not shown it.

The aggregate in sample_cpu averages the raw idle delta (metrics.c:157) while cpu_pct_from_idle clamps its by-value copy to elapsed (metrics.c:90). In the slack band the per-core value is a clamped 0 % but the aggregate still subtracts the overshoot, so the average can read below the displayed cores by up to the slack (~0.5 points per fully idle core at 10 Hz). Bounded and cosmetic. The duplicated rounding/clamp at metrics.c:94-99 and :165-170 (demoted from a maintainability P3) is where the two paths can drift.

There is no upper bound on elapsed. A multi-second gap (LiveArea/standby, debugger pause, a long stall) is averaged as if it were one 100 ms window; if sceKernelGetProcessTimeWide and the idle clocks disagree across standby, the first post-resume sample is either a fabricated ~100 % pushed into the trace or a rejected sample that blanks the row for two windows.

PLATFORM_CPU_COUNT (4) mirrors the SDK's cpuInfo[4] with no static assertion, and platform_read_cpu() loops the port constant over the SDK array (platform_psp2.c:186). A future bump to the port count would read past the struct; a _Static_assert on sizeof(info.cpuInfo)/sizeof(info.cpuInfo[0]) in the adapter would pin it.

sceKernelGetSystemInfo is a strong SceLibKernel import, so a missing NID on 3.65 fails at module load instead of degrading to `--`. The [C] tag documents the risk, but fail-closed policy cannot cover an unresolved import.

agent-wiki/04-userland-apps.md "Power and clocks" was not updated with the sceKernelGetSystemInfo CPU-load route, so the wiki's app-facing API reference still omits the one userland CPU source the project now relies on.

The [C] idle-clock unit and the adapter's four refusal paths (sceKernelGetSystemInfo < 0, activeCpuMask == 0, time_us == 0, all idle clocks zero) can only be settled on the 3.65 console; the host fake emits microsecond deltas by construction, so no host test can distinguish a unit mismatch from real load.

The unused-symbol claims behind #5 were established by text search only (callsite completeness: grep-only); a macro-generated or build-time reference would not appear. No out-of-tree consumer exists in the workspace.
testing_gaps: Rate tests cannot distinguish per-tick from per-second (demoted from a testing P2): every fake read advances exactly 100 ms (FAKE_CPU_STEP_US, fake_platform.c:38), so replacing cpu_rate()'s body with `delta * 10` still prints 145 checks, 0 failures. The app's slow tick is a frame accumulator with catch-up samples, so the real interval drifts; a configurable fake step plus a 500 ms case would pin it and would give fake_set_cpu_activity a caller.

Counter-reset guards are untested: metrics.c:147 (idle_us < prev) and metrics.c:178/181 (ctx_switches/wakeups >= prev) exist to stop an underflow, but the fake has no setter for a decreasing counter, so deleting either guard would leave the suite green.

cpu_pct_from_idle's slack path (metrics.c:82-91) is unexercised: only idle = 2 x elapsed is tested, not the accept-and-clamp case where a fully idle core's idle clock reads a few microseconds past the wall clock and must render 0 %, not `--`; the unclamped value also feeds idle_sum, which is where the aggregate mismatch comes from.
The baseline-only state after metrics_init() is not asserted: cpu_valid must be 0, every core CPU_CORE_UNKNOWN and hist_cpu empty until a second window exists.

Recovery after a failed or rejected CPU sample is untested: test_cpu_failed_read_leaves_trace_alone stops at the failure, so the two-window blank that follows a cleared baseline is unpinned and a regression that never resumes the trace would pass.
No test narrows activeCpuMask between samples (or wraps a 32-bit threadSwitchCount), so the regression path behind #2 and the mask-intersection behaviour are unverified.
All four active cores at 100 % (every idle delta zero) must yield a valid 100 average rather than `--`; test_cpu_active_mask covers only a single 100 % core.
The aggregate's +0.5 rounding is unpinned: the fixture's mean is 13.25, which truncates to the same 13, so a switch to plain truncation would still pass; a mean like 13.5 would distinguish them.

The diff removed test_failed_memory_leaves_trace_alone and replaced it with the CPU equivalent; fake_set_memory_absent() now only feeds test_alert_policy, so nothing asserts mem_valid == 0 or that the three pools render `--` after a failed memory read. This is a coverage regression in the memory subsystem, reported as a gap rather than a finding because no reviewer assigned it a severity.

triage_groups.title: Fail-closed CPU readout
triage_groups.context: #1 leaves one direction of an idle-clock unit error undetected while four docs promise it is caught; #2 draws CTX/WAKE 0/S when the cumulative counters are unavailable.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Decide #1 first - correct the docs to the one-sided guarantee or add the opposite-direction guard - then implement #2's per-rate validity flags so the caption follows the same `--` contract.
triage_groups.why: Both are one honesty failure: a value the platform cannot support is drawn as a measurement. #1's decision fixes the wording and checklist that #2's tests and docs will follow.

triage_groups.title: Verification claims vs. actual coverage
triage_groups.context: #3: no test or preview exercises the panel's `--` branch. #7: the [V] ledger marks the fixed 0-100 % trace host-test verified although no test observes the axis.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Do #3 first (preview scene plus a pure formatting helper the harness links), then correct #7's rows to what is actually asserted.
triage_groups.why: Both let the docs claim verification the suite cannot produce; the added coverage shrinks what #7 has to reword.

triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Mechanical edits in any order: add core/metrics.c to the [C] row's Where column, add CPU to the header comment, and reduce the Next cell to the flash-and-confirm step.
